# Introduction

This document includes the differential gene expression analysis (DEA) for the gene, transcript and exon expression of the postmortem human brain (dorsolateral prefrontal cortex - Brodmann area 9) samples coming from patients with schizophrenia (SCZ), bipolar disorder (BIP) and major depression disorder (MDD) as well as healthy controls (CTL). We decided to combine all diagnosis (SCZ, BIP and MDD) to one case (CASE) for power reasons. We did not find any differentially expressed genes, transcripts or exons using the diagnosis as single cases. Following steps are performed for each level (1. genes, 2. transcripts and 3. exons):

1. DEA for diagnosis correcting for all covariates
2. DEA for diagnosis and sex*diagnosis interaction model
3. DEA using the polygenic risk score instead of the diagnosis (also correcting for covariates)

For the transcript and exon level, we also include a 4. and 5. step, there we repeat step 1. and 3. from above with a recalculated FDR based on the included gene-level, meaning that only the transcript/exon with the best P-value per gene is taken into account. 


# Packages 

Below you can find the list of packages required by the workflow. 
```{r}
# General Bioconductor packages

library(oligo)

# Formatting packages

library(dplyr)

library(plyr)
```


# Paths

Before we can start, we need to make sure that all necessary paths and folder names are saved. If the output folder does not exist yet, we will generate it using the systems (Red Hat Enterprise Linux operating system: Fedora 25) "mkdir" command. 
```{r}

rdata_path <- "/storage/groups/ccm01/workspace/MPIP-Dean_postmortem_brain/04.DEA/01_RData_files"

system(paste0("mkdir -p ", outpath))
```


# Functions

As we have to do several analysis multiple times, we will put these into functions to reduce the lines of code. 
```{r definition, echo = F}
# function to load the PRS all score file, change the colnames into right order and return only IID and 0.01 PRS
GetPRS <- function(filename){
  all_scores <- suppressWarnings(fread(filename, stringsAsFactors = F))
  # set colnames right 
  names <- colnames(all_scores)[-1] # remove first colname and save all others
  all_scores$`1` <- NULL # remove last column with NAs
  colnames(all_scores) <- names # set right colnames
  # return only IID and PRS for 0.01
  if ("0.01" %in% colnames(all_scores)) {
    score <- all_scores[, c("IID", "0.01")]
    return(score)
  } else {
    # if two thresholds have the same amount of SNPs PRSice-2 does only print one
    # for BMI-2015 (GIANT) no 0.01 value is given as it has the same SNP number as 0.00995005, so we will take this PRS instead!
    score <- all_scores[, c("IID", "0.00995005")]
  }
  return(score)
}

# function to run the linear model (limma) using the normal model for genes only 
RunLimma <- function(design, summary){
  # get top DE genes
  fit <- lmFit(summary, design)
  fit2 <- eBayes(fit)
  return(fit2)
}

# functions to generate result tables
# 1. get top hits
# 2. rename columns
# 3. separate merged gene symbols and remove duplicated rows: necessary as exactly the same gene symbols (and IDs for transcript/exon level) were merged together. This happens because:
# on gene level: one of the transripts of the gene is an uncharacterized protein and therefore leads to two different gene ensembl IDs
# on transcript/exon level: two or more transcripts/exons have the exact same expression values and were merged together as also done for their gene symbols and IDs. Usually these gene symbols and IDs are just duplicates and we need to remove these for further analysis (e.g. new FDR correction). The merged transcript/exon IDs we will leave merged.
# 4. save the resulting table into an output file
GenerateResultTableGene <- function(fit, variable, file){
  top_hits <- topTable(fit, confint = 0.95, coef = variable, adjust = "BH", number = Inf)
  print(top_hits[1:2, ])
  print(paste0("log2FC range: ", round(min(top_hits$logFC), 2), " until ", round(max(top_hits$logFC), 2)))
  colnames(top_hits) <- c("Ensembl Gene ID", "Location", "Gene Symbol", "LogFC", "95% Confidence Interval, lower bound", "95% Confidence Interval, upper bound", "Average Expression", "T-statistic", "P-value", "FDR estimate", "Log-odds Ratio")
  top_hits <- unique(as.data.frame(separate_rows(top_hits, `Ensembl Gene ID`, sep = "\\|")))
  top_hits <- unique(as.data.frame(separate_rows(top_hits, `Gene Symbol`, sep = "\\|")))
  write.table(top_hits, file = paste0(outpath, "/", file), sep = "\t", row.names = F)
  return(top_hits)
}
GenerateResultTableTranscript <- function(fit, variable, file){
  top_hits <- topTable(fit, confint = 0.95, coef = variable, adjust = "BH", number = Inf)
  print(top_hits[1:2, ])
  print(paste0("log2FC range: ", round(min(top_hits$logFC), 2), " until ", round(max(top_hits$logFC), 2)))
  colnames(top_hits) <- c("Ensembl Transcript ID", "Location", "Ensembl Gene ID", "Gene Symbol", "LogFC", "95% Confidence Interval, lower bound", "95% Confidence Interval, upper bound", "Average Expression", "T-statistic", "P-value", "FDR estimate", "Log-odds Ratio")
  top_hits <- unique(as.data.frame(separate_rows(top_hits, `Ensembl Gene ID`, sep = "\\|")))
  top_hits <- unique(as.data.frame(separate_rows(top_hits, `Gene Symbol`, sep = "\\|")))
  write.table(top_hits, file = paste0(outpath, "/", file), sep = "\t", row.names = F)
  return(top_hits)
}
GenerateResultTableExon <- function(fit, variable, file){
  top_hits <- topTable(fit, confint = 0.95, coef = variable, adjust = "BH", number = Inf)
  print(top_hits[1:2, ])
  print(paste0("log2FC range: ", round(min(top_hits$logFC), 2), " until ", round(max(top_hits$logFC), 2)))
  colnames(top_hits) <- c("Ensembl Exon ID", "Location", "Ensembl Transcript ID", "Ensembl Gene ID", "Gene Symbol", "LogFC", "95% Confidence Interval, lower bound", "95% Confidence Interval, upper bound", "Average Expression", "T-statistic", "P-value", "FDR estimate", "Log-odds Ratio")
  top_hits <- unique(as.data.frame(separate_rows(top_hits, `Ensembl Gene ID`, sep = "\\|")))
  top_hits <- unique(as.data.frame(separate_rows(top_hits, `Gene Symbol`, sep = "\\|")))
  write.table(top_hits, file = paste0(outpath, "/", file), sep = "\t", row.names = F)
  return(top_hits)
}

# function to recalculate the P-value and fdr for transcripts and exons based on gene level (Ensmebl Gene ID NOT Symbol!!): load the result table, get the smallest P-value for a gene (Ensembl Gene ID), calculate new fdr using the genes smallest P-values and gene number as background
GetExprWithSmallestP <- function(input, summaries){
  res <- fread(paste0(outpath, "/", input), header = T, stringsAsFactors = F)
  # get the rows with the lowest P-value per gene ID
  min_pval <- res[ , .SD[which.min(`P-value`)], by = `Ensembl Gene ID`]
  # get all transcript/exon IDs with lowest P-value per gene ID
  index <- which(rownames(exprs(summaries)) %in% as.character(c(min_pval[, 2])[[1]]))
  # reduce transcript/exon_summaries to these transcripts/exons
  summaries <- summaries[c(index), ]
  dim(summaries)
  return(summaries)
}
```


# Load data

## Microarray expression

Now, we will load the normalized and batch corrected microarray data summarized to gene, transcript and exon level. 
```{r, echo = F}
# Import RMA corrected and annotated Affymetrix microarray data on gene level (from probesets)
load(paste0(rdata_path, "/7_affymetrix_exon_microarray_data_after_rma_probeset_summaries_filtered_batch_corrected_SVA_gene_summaries_annotated.RData"))
exprs(gene_summaries) <- as.matrix(exprs(gene_summaries))
dim(gene_summaries)
# Import RMA corrected and annotated Affymetrix microarray data on transcript level
load(paste0(rdata_path, "/7_affymetrix_exon_microarray_data_after_rma_probeset_summaries_filtered_batch_corrected_SVA_transcript_summaries_annotated.RData"))
exprs(transcript_summaries) <- as.matrix(exprs(transcript_summaries))
dim(transcript_summaries)
# Import RMA corrected and annotated Affymetrix microarray data on exon level
load(paste0(rdata_path, "/7_affymetrix_exon_microarray_data_after_rma_probeset_summaries_filtered_batch_corrected_SVA_exon_summaries_annotated.RData"))
exprs(exon_summaries) <- as.matrix(exprs(exon_summaries))
dim(exon_summaries)
# save pData into an extra variable (use pData of probeset genes as it includes SV1)
pData <- pData(gene_summaries)
```

## Polygenic risk scores

# Differential Gene Expression Analysis

Now, we calculate the differentially expressed genes, transcripts and exons using a linear mixed model (limma package) correcting for all the covariates. We will also generate output tables and RData files for all results.

## Gene level

### Diagnosis with normal model

First, we run the linear model with correction for all covariates and generate the result table. 
```{r, echo = F}
# generate design matrix
design <- model.matrix(~ Dx + Age + Sex + pH + PMI + RIN + RIN2 + Suicide + Type_of_Death + C1 + C2 + C3 + C4 + SV1, pData)
# differential expression analysis (limma)
fit <- RunLimma(design, gene_summaries)
# get residuals
res <- residuals.MArrayLM(fit, exprs(gene_summaries))
# result tables
top_hits <- GenerateResultTableGene(fit, variable = "DxCASE", file =  "1.1_diff_expr_genes_for_diagnosis.csv")
top_hits_age <- GenerateResultTableGene(fit, variable = "Age", file =  "1.1_diff_expr_genes_for_age.csv")
top_hits_ph <- GenerateResultTableGene(fit, variable = "pH", file =  "1.1_diff_expr_genes_for_ph.csv")
top_hits_pmi <- GenerateResultTableGene(fit, variable = "PMI", file =  "1.1_diff_expr_genes_for_pmi.csv")
top_hits_c2 <- GenerateResultTableGene(fit, variable = "C2", file =  "1.1_diff_expr_genes_for_pc2.csv")
top_hits_c1 <- GenerateResultTableGene(fit, variable = "C1", file =  "1.1_diff_expr_genes_for_pc1.csv")
top_hits_rin <- GenerateResultTableGene(fit, variable = "RIN", file =  "1.1_diff_expr_genes_for_rin.csv")
top_hits_rin2 <- GenerateResultTableGene(fit, variable = "RIN2", file =  "1.1_diff_expr_genes_for_rin2.csv")
# save data into an RData file (for figure generation)
save(design, fit, top_hits, res, file = paste0(outpath, "/1.1_diff_expr_genes_for_diagnosis.RData"))
# remove unnecessary data
rm(fit, design, res)
```
We can find `r length(unique(top_hits[top_hits$"FDR estimate" < 0.1, "Ensembl Gene ID"]))` hits for diagnosis, `r length(unique(top_hits_age[top_hits_age$"FDR estimate" < 0.1, "Ensembl Gene ID"]))` hits for age, `r length(unique(top_hits_ph[top_hits_ph$"FDR estimate" < 0.1, "Ensembl Gene ID"]))` hits for pH, `r length(unique(top_hits_pmi[top_hits_pmi$"FDR estimate" < 0.1, "Ensembl Gene ID"]))` hits for PMI, `r length(unique(top_hits_rin[top_hits_rin$"FDR estimate" < 0.1, "Ensembl Gene ID"]))` hits for RIN, `r length(unique(top_hits_rin2[top_hits_rin2$"FDR estimate" < 0.1, "Ensembl Gene ID"]))` hits for RIN2, `r length(unique(top_hits_c1[top_hits_c1$"FDR estimate" < 0.1, "Ensembl Gene ID"]))` hits for the first ancestry dimension (PC1) and `r length(unique(top_hits_c2[top_hits_c2$"FDR estimate" < 0.1, "Ensembl Gene ID"]))` hits for the second ancestry dimension (PC2).  

### Diagnosis with sex and diagnosis interaction model

Adding (Dx*Sex) to the model.
```{r, echo = F}
# generate design matrix
design <- model.matrix(~ Dx + Age + Sex + pH + PMI + RIN + RIN2 + Suicide + Type_of_Death + C1 + C2 + C3 + C4 + SV1 + (Sex * Dx), pData)
# differential expression analysis (limma)
fit <- RunLimma(design, gene_summaries)
# result table
top_hits <- GenerateResultTableGene(fit, variable = "DxCASE", file =  "1.2_diff_expr_genes_for_diagnosis_with_sex_dx_interaction.csv")
# save data into an RData file (for figure generation)
save(design, fit, top_hits, file = paste0(outpath, "/1.2_diff_expr_genes_for_diagnosis_with_sex_dx_interaction.RData"))
# remove unnecessary data
rm(fit, design)
```
We can find `r length(unique(top_hits[top_hits$"FDR estimate" < 0.1, "Ensembl Gene ID"]))` hits for diagnosis. The hit has the gene name: `r top_hits[top_hits$"FDR estimate" < 0.1, "Ensembl Gene ID"]`. 

### PRS with normal model (eQTS)

Now, we use the polygenic risk scores based on GWAS summary statistics instead of the diagnosis as input. As the PRS is a continuous (numeric) covariate and diagnosis is a categorical (CASE/CTL) covariate the fold change/log2 fold change (logFC) can not be calculated correctly, therefore, generating volcano plots does not make sense for PRS based differentially expressed analyses (DEA). We will use the PRSs based on the GWAS of following disorders: ADHD-2019, ASD-2019, BIP-2019, BMI-2015, CAD-2017, CDG1-2013, CDG2-2019, EA-2018, HE-2014, IN-2018, MDD1-2012, MDD2-2018, MDD3-2019, SCZ2-2014, SCZ3-2020 and T2D-2017. As we combine genotype results with expression, this is also called expression quantitative trait score (eQTS).

**ADHD-2019 PRS**
```{r, echo = F}
# generate design matrix
design <- model.matrix(~ PRS.ADHD + Age + Sex + pH + PMI + RIN + RIN2 + Suicide + Type_of_Death + C1 + C2 + C3 + C4 + SV1, pData)
# differential expression analysis (limma)
fit <- RunLimma(design, gene_summaries)
# generate result table
top_hits <- GenerateResultTableGene(fit, variable = "PRS.ADHD", file =  "1.3.1_diff_expr_genes_for_ADHD-2019_PRS.csv")
# remove data, to reduce errors based on wrong data outputs
rm(design, fit)
```
We can find `r length(unique(top_hits[top_hits$"FDR estimate" < 0.1, "Ensembl Gene ID"]))` hits for the ADHD-2019 PRS.

```{r, echo = F}
# differential expression analysis (limma)
fit <- RunLimma(design, gene_summaries)
# generate result table
```

## Transcript level

### Diagnosis with normal model

First, run the linear model with correction for all covariates and generate the result table. 
```{r, echo = F}
# generate design matrix
design <- model.matrix(~ Dx + Age + Sex + pH + PMI + RIN + RIN2 + Suicide + Type_of_Death + C1 + C2 + C3 + C4 + SV1, pData)
# differential expression analysis (limma)
fit <- RunLimma(design, transcript_summaries)
# result table
top_hits <- GenerateResultTableTranscript(fit, variable = "DxCASE", file =  "2.1_diff_expr_transcripts_for_diagnosis.csv")
# get residuals
res <- residuals.MArrayLM(fit, exprs(transcript_summaries))
# save data into an RData file (for figure generation)
save(design, fit, top_hits, res, file = paste0(outpath, "/2.1_diff_expr_transcripts_for_diagnosis.RData"))
# remove unnecessary data
rm(fit, design, res)
```
No (`r length(unique(top_hits[top_hits$"FDR estimate" < 0.1, "Ensembl Gene ID"]))`) hits. Maybe a problem of the multiple testing correction as we have too many transcripts to correct for. We will test a new FDR correction model in the following section.

### Diagnosis with sex and diagnosis interaction model

Adding (Dx*Sex) to the model.
```{r, echo = F}
# generate design matrix
design <- model.matrix(~ Dx + Age + Sex + pH + PMI + RIN + RIN2 + Suicide + Type_of_Death + C1 + C2 + C3 + C4 + SV1 + (Sex*Dx), pData)
# differential expression analysis (limma)
fit <- RunLimma(design, transcript_summaries)
# result table
top_hits <- GenerateResultTableTranscript(fit, variable = "DxCASE", file =  "2.2_diff_expr_transcripts_for_diagnosis_with_sex_dx_interaction.csv")
# save data into an RData file (for figure generation)
save(design, fit, top_hits, file = paste0(outpath, "/2.2_diff_expr_transcripts_for_diagnosis_with_sex_dx_interaction.RData"))
# remove unnecessary data
rm(fit, design)
```
No (`r length(unique(top_hits[top_hits$"FDR estimate" < 0.1, "Ensembl Gene ID"]))`) hits. Maybe also a problem of the multiple testing correction as we have too many transcripts to correct for.

### Diagnosis with recalculated P-values and FDR

As the low adjusted P-values of the transcript expressions could come from the high number of transcripts to test for, we want to redo the adjusted P-value calculation as followed:

1. Take the lowest P-value of all transcripts corresponding to a gene
2. Get all transcript IDs and reduce the expression Set to these transcripts
2. Calculate P-values and FDR using limma on the reduced transcript set
```{r, echo = F}
# reduce expression set
dim(transcript_summaries)
transcript_summaries_new <- GetExprWithSmallestP(input = "2.1_diff_expr_transcripts_for_diagnosis.csv", transcript_summaries)
dim(transcript_summaries_new)
# generate design matrix
design <- model.matrix(~ Dx + Age + Sex + pH + PMI + RIN + RIN2 + Suicide + Type_of_Death + C1 + C2 + C3 + C4 + SV1, pData)
# differential expression analysis (limma)
fit <- RunLimma(design, transcript_summaries_new)
# get residuals
res <- residuals.MArrayLM(fit, exprs(transcript_summaries_new))
# result table
top_hits <- GenerateResultTableTranscript(fit, variable = "DxCASE", file =  "2.4_diff_expr_transcripts_for_diagnosis_new_pvalue_and_fdr.csv")
top_hits_age <- GenerateResultTableTranscript(fit, variable = "Age", file =  "2.4_diff_expr_transcripts_for_age_new_pvalue_and_fdr.csv")
top_hits_ph <- GenerateResultTableTranscript(fit, variable = "pH", file =  "2.4_diff_expr_transcripts_for_ph_new_pvalue_and_fdr.csv")
top_hits_pmi <- GenerateResultTableTranscript(fit, variable = "PMI", file =  "2.4_diff_expr_transcripts_for_pmi_new_pvalue_and_fdr.csv")
top_hits_c2 <- GenerateResultTableTranscript(fit, variable = "C2", file =  "2.4_diff_expr_transcripts_for_c2_new_pvalue_and_fdr.csv")
top_hits_c1 <- GenerateResultTableTranscript(fit, variable = "C1", file =  "2.4_diff_expr_transcripts_for_c1_new_pvalue_and_fdr.csv")
# save data into an RData file (for figure generation)
save(design, fit, top_hits, res, file = paste0(outpath, "/2.4_diff_expr_transcripts_for_diagnosis_new_pvalue_and_fdr.RData"))
# remove unnecessary data
rm(fit, design)
```
Now, we have multiple hits on the transcript level. We can find `r length(unique(top_hits[top_hits$"FDR estimate" < 0.1, "Ensembl Gene ID"]))` hits for diagnosis, `r length(unique(top_hits_age[top_hits_age$"FDR estimate" < 0.1, "Ensembl Gene ID"]))` hits for age, `r length(unique(top_hits_ph[top_hits_ph$"FDR estimate" < 0.1, "Ensembl Gene ID"]))` hits for pH, `r length(unique(top_hits_pmi[top_hits_pmi$"FDR estimate" < 0.1, "Ensembl Gene ID"]))` hits for pmi, `r length(unique(top_hits_c2[top_hits_c2$"FDR estimate" < 0.1, "Ensembl Gene ID"]))` hits for the second ancestry principal component (PC2). All hits are based on a 10% FDR (FDR < 0.1). The six diagnosis gene hits are: `r top_hits[top_hits$"FDR estimate" < 0.1, "Ensembl Gene ID"]`

### Diagnosis with sex and diagnosis interaction model with recalculated P-values and FDR

Adding (Dx*Sex) to the model.
```{r, echo = F}
# reduce expression set
transcript_summaries_new <- GetExprWithSmallestP(input = "2.2_diff_expr_transcripts_for_diagnosis_with_sex_dx_interaction.csv", transcript_summaries)
dim(transcript_summaries_new)
# generate design matrix
design <- model.matrix(~ Dx + Age + Sex + pH + PMI + RIN + RIN2 + Suicide + Type_of_Death + C1 + C2 + C3 + C4 + SV1 + (Sex*Dx), pData)
# differential expression analysis (limma)
fit <- RunLimma(design, transcript_summaries_new)
# generate result table
top_hits <- GenerateResultTableTranscript(fit, variable = "DxCASE", file =  "2.4_diff_expr_transcripts_for_diagnosis_with_sex_dx_interaction_new_pvalue_and_fdr.csv")
# save data into an RData file (for figure generation)
save(design, fit, top_hits, file = paste0(outpath, "/2.4_diff_expr_transcripts_for_diagnosis_with_sex_dx_interaction_new_pvalue_and_fdr.RData"))
# remove unnecessary data
rm(transcript_summaries_new, design, fit)
```
Now, we have (`r length(unique(top_hits[top_hits$"FDR estimate" < 0.1, "Ensembl Gene ID"]))`) hits. The (`r length(unique(top_hits[top_hits$"FDR estimate" < 0.1, "Ensembl Gene ID"]))`) sex and diagnosis interaction gene hits are: `r top_hits[top_hits$"FDR estimate" < 0.1, "Ensembl Gene ID"]`.

### PRS with recalculated P-value and FDR

As the low adjusted P-values of the transcript expressions could come from the high number of transcripts to test for, we want to redo the adjusted P-value calculation for all PRS from above as follows:

1. Take the lowest P-value of all transcripts corresponding to a gene
2. Get all transcript IDs and reduce the expression Set to these transcripts
2. Calculate P-values and FDR using limma on the reduced transcript set

**ADHD-2019 PRS**

```{r, echo = F}
fit <- RunLimma(design, transcript_summaries_new)
# generate result table
top_hits <- GenerateResultTableTranscript(fit, variable = "PRS.ADHD", file =  "2.5.1_diff_expr_transcripts_for_ADHD-2019_PRS_new_pvalue_and_fdr.csv")
# remove unnecessary data
rm(transcript_summaries_new, design, fit)
```
We can find `r length(unique(top_hits[top_hits$"FDR estimate" < 0.1, "Ensembl Gene ID"]))` hits for FDR < 10% (hits for FDR < 5%: `r length(unique(top_hits[top_hits$"FDR estimate" < 0.05, "Ensembl Gene ID"]))`) for the ADHD-2019 PRS.

## Exon level 

### Diagnosis with normal model

First, run the linear model with correction for all covariates and generate the result table. 
```{r, echo = F}
# generate design matrix
design <- model.matrix(~ Dx + Age + Sex + pH + PMI + RIN + RIN2 + Suicide + Type_of_Death + C1 + C2 + C3 + C4 + SV1, pData)
# differential expression analysis (limma)
fit <- RunLimma(design, exon_summaries)
# result table
top_hits <- GenerateResultTableExon(fit, variable = "DxCASE", file =  "3.1_diff_expr_exons_for_diagnosis.csv")
# get residuals
res <- residuals.MArrayLM(fit, exprs(exon_summaries))
# save data into an RData file (for figure generation)
save(design, fit, top_hits, res, file = paste0(outpath, "/3.1_diff_expr_exons_for_diagnosis.RData"))
# remove unnecessary data
rm(fit, design, res)
```
We can find `r length(unique(top_hits[top_hits$"FDR estimate" < 0.1, "Ensembl Gene ID"]))` hits for diagnosis. Maybe it is a multiple testing correction problem as we have a lot of exons (around 200,000). 

### Diagnosis with sex and diagnosis interaction model

Adding a Sex and diagnosis interaction term (Sex * Dx) to the model.
```{r, echo = F}
# generate design matrix
design <- model.matrix(~ Dx + Age + Sex + pH + PMI + RIN + RIN2 + Suicide + Type_of_Death + C1 + C2 + C3 + C4 + SV1 + (Sex*Dx), pData)
# differential expression analysis (limma)
fit <- RunLimma(design, exon_summaries)
# result table
top_hits <- GenerateResultTableExon(fit, variable = "DxCASE", file =  "3.2_diff_expr_exons_for_diagnosis_with_sex_dx_interaction.csv")
# save data into an RData file (for figure generation)
save(design, fit, top_hits, file = paste0(outpath, "/3.2_diff_expr_exons_for_diagnosis_with_sex_dx_interaction.RData"))
# remove unnecessary data
rm(fit, design)
```
No `r length(unique(top_hits[top_hits$"FDR estimate" < 0.1, "Ensembl Gene ID"]))` hits. Maybe also a problem of the multiple testing correction.

### Diagnosis with recalculated P-values and FDR

As the low adjusted P-values of the transcript expressions could come from the high number of transcripts to test for, we want to redo the adjusted P-value calculation as followed:

1. Take the lowest P-value of all transcripts corresponding to a gene
2. Get all transcript IDs and reduce the expression Set to these transcripts
2. Calculate P-values and FDR using limma on the reduced transcript set
```{r, echo = F}
# reduce expression set
dim(exon_summaries)
exon_summaries_new <- GetExprWithSmallestP(input = "3.1_diff_expr_exons_for_diagnosis.csv", exon_summaries)
dim(exon_summaries_new)
# generate design matrix
design <- model.matrix(~ Dx + Age + Sex + pH + PMI + RIN + RIN2 + Suicide + Type_of_Death + C1 + C2 + C3 + C4 + SV1, pData)
# differential expression analysis (limma)
fit <- RunLimma(design, exon_summaries_new)
# get residuals
res <- residuals.MArrayLM(fit, exprs(exon_summaries_new))
# result table
top_hits <- GenerateResultTableExon(fit, variable = "DxCASE", file =  "3.4_diff_expr_exons_for_diagnosis_new_pvalue_and_fdr.csv")
top_hits_age <- GenerateResultTableExon(fit, variable = "Age", file =  "3.4_diff_expr_exons_for_age_new_pvalue_and_fdr.csv")
top_hits_ph <- GenerateResultTableExon(fit, variable = "pH", file =  "3.4_diff_expr_exons_for_ph_new_pvalue_and_fdr.csv")
top_hits_pmi <- GenerateResultTableExon(fit, variable = "PMI", file =  "3.4_diff_expr_exons_for_pmi_new_pvalue_and_fdr.csv")
top_hits_c2 <- GenerateResultTableExon(fit, variable = "C2", file =  "3.4_diff_expr_exons_for_c2_new_pvalue_and_fdr.csv")
top_hits_c1 <- GenerateResultTableExon(fit, variable = "C1", file =  "3.4_diff_expr_exons_for_c1_new_pvalue_and_fdr.csv")
# save data into an RData file (for figure generation)
save(design, fit, top_hits, res, file = paste0(outpath, "/3.4_diff_expr_exons_for_diagnosis_new_pvalue_and_fdr.RData"))
# remove unnecessary data
rm(fit, design)
```
Now, we have multiple hits on the exon level. We can find `r length(unique(top_hits[top_hits$"FDR estimate" < 0.1, "Ensembl Gene ID"]))` hits for diagnosis, `r length(unique(top_hits_age[top_hits_age$"FDR estimate" < 0.1, "Ensembl Gene ID"]))` hits for age, `r length(unique(top_hits_ph[top_hits_ph$"FDR estimate" < 0.1, "Ensembl Gene ID"]))` hits for pH, `r length(unique(top_hits_pmi[top_hits_pmi$"FDR estimate" < 0.1, "Ensembl Gene ID"]))` hits for pmi, `r length(unique(top_hits_c2[top_hits_c2$"FDR estimate" < 0.1, "Ensembl Gene ID"]))` hits for the second ancestry principal component (PC2). All hits are based on a 10% FDR (FDR < 0.1). The first ten diagnosis gene hits are: `r top_hits[top_hits$"FDR estimate" < 0.1, "Ensembl Gene ID"][1:10]`

### Diagnosis with sex and diagnosis interaction model with recalculated P-values and FDR

Adding a Sex and diagnosis interaction term (Sex * Dx) to the model.
```{r, echo = F}
# reduce expression set
exon_summaries_new <- GetExprWithSmallestP(input = "3.2_diff_expr_exons_for_diagnosis_with_sex_dx_interaction.csv", exon_summaries)
dim(exon_summaries_new)
# generate design matrix
design <- model.matrix(~ Dx + Age + Sex + pH + PMI + RIN + RIN2 + Suicide + Type_of_Death + C1 + C2 + C3 + C4 + SV1 + (Sex*Dx), pData)
# differential expression analysis (limma)
fit <- RunLimma(design, exon_summaries_new)
# generate result table
top_hits <- GenerateResultTableExon(fit, variable = "DxCASE", file =  "3.4_diff_expr_exons_for_diagnosis_with_sex_dx_interaction_new_pvalue_and_fdr.csv")
# save data into an RData file (for figure generation)
save(design, fit, top_hits, file = paste0(outpath, "/3.4_diff_expr_exons_for_diagnosis_with_sex_dx_interaction_new_pvalue_and_fdr.RData"))
# remove unnecessary data
rm(exon_summaries_new, design, fit)
```
Now, we have multiple hits on the exon level. We can find `r length(unique(top_hits[top_hits$"FDR estimate" < 0.1, "Ensembl Gene ID"]))` hits for diagnosis and sex interaction. The first ten diagnosis gene hits are: `r top_hits[top_hits$"FDR estimate" < 0.1, "Ensembl Gene ID"][1:10]`
